scenario: A national cyber-security agency selects incident responders who are expert in malware reverse-engineering OR in live-network forensics. The two skills are independent in the talent pool; OR-gate hiring produces a negative collider correlation within the response unit.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (malware reverse-engineering) OR (live-network forensics)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(malware_analysis | ¬network_forensics, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(malware_analysis | network_forensics, selected) and show it equals P(malware_analysis). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between malware reverse-engineering and live-network forensics.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks live-network forensics must possess malware reverse-engineering to be admitted — hence P(malware_analysis|¬network_forensics,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has live-network forensics is admitted regardless of malware reverse-engineering, so P(malware_analysis|network_forensics,sel)=P(malware_analysis)=0.43. The gap (1.0 vs 0.43) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between malware reverse-engineering and live-network forensics observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.43+0.47-0.43×0.47=0.6979. (2) Among candidates without live-network forensics: only those with malware reverse-engineering are selected → P(malware_analysis|¬network_forensics,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with live-network forensics: selected regardless of malware reverse-engineering → P(malware_analysis|network_forensics,sel)=P(malware_analysis)=0.43. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬network_forensics raises P(malware_analysis) from 0.43 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.43,0.47
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6979)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.43)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
